title: Headroom Spillway & Rack Slot Matrix — GPU Pool Slotting Plan
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to decide how we slot GPUs across on-prem racks for upcoming Q4 capacity growth, with explicit thermal and electrical "spillway" (headroom) targets for transient bursts and single-PDU failures. This is a pragmatic plan for the EU cluster (primary colocation) with knobs for US and APAC follow-ups.

Summary (one paragraph):
We have 48 new A100-equivalent GPUs arriving in Oct. Current available racks (A1..A6) have heterogeneous PDU and CRAC headroom. This sheet models three slotting strategies (compact, balanced, conservative) and a spillway policy (reserve kW and cooling to allow 20% transient oversubscribe for up to 90s). Baseline recommendation: balanced slotting + 15% thermal spillway across the populated rack set, enable cross-rack burst routing for latency-tolerant workloads.

Assumptions:
- GPU thermal draw per full-power card: 0.35 kW (350 W) steady, 0.55 kW transient (90s) during max bursts.
- Rack overhead (host/psu/switch): 1.2 kW per rack nominal.
- CRAC cooling margin must be >= 12% for sustained <1 hour spikes; spillway target is 15% for safety.
- Single PDU failure target: operate at 60% of pre-failure capacity (i.e., plan live migration / fallback triggers at 60% utilization).
- Power utility headroom for colo cage: 80 kW available net before additional contract required.
- Target utilization on inference pools: 55% average, 85% burstable for short periods.

Rack matrix (current measured values, taken 2026-08-10 acoustic & power sweep):
RackID,InstalledGPUs,MaxPDU_kW,AvailablePDUHeadroom_kW,CoolingLoopHeadroom_kW,PlannedAdditionalSlots,PreferredStrategyNotes
A1,8,12.0,4.4,3.2,4,good PDU redundancy (2x) - balanced fill
A2,12,14.0,1.4,1.0,2,near PDU limit - conservative slot only 2
A3,0,10.0,9.0,5.8,8,empty rack - candidate for compact fill
A4,6,11.0,3.0,2.4,4,shared CRAC loop with A5 - avoid stacking hotspots
A5,10,13.0,2.1,1.6,6,cooling loop slightly warmer - spread GPUs across mid U positions
A6,4,9.0,4.6,3.5,4,newer rack PDUs - good transient headroom

Derived capacity (simple math):
- Total spare PDU headroom (sum): 24.5 kW -> nominal spare GPU slots (at 0.35 kW steady) = floor(24.5 / 0.35) = 70 slots (theoretical)
- But cooling loop headroom total: 17.5 kW -> cooling-limited slots = floor(17.5 / 0.35) = 50 slots
- Practical limit (respecting spillway and single-PDU failure): apply 15% spillway -> cooling-limited practical slots = floor(50 * 0.85) = 42 slots

Slotting strategies compared (for 48 new cards):
- Compact (maximize density): target racks A3, A5, A1 first. Pros: fewer racks to maintain. Cons: localized thermal hotspots, higher single-failure blast radius.
- Balanced (spread evenly with awareness of PDU/cooling): distribute across A1, A3, A4, A6 primarily, only 2 into A2/A5 because they are closer to PDU/cooling limits. Pros: resilient, preserves cooling margins. Cons: slightly more networking / cabling overhead.
- Conservative (limit per-rack to <60% PDU utilization): only fill A3, A6, and add a temporary remote rack (procure) if more than 28 slots needed. Pros: minimal risk. Cons: requires extra rack or delaying rollout.

Failure & burst scenarios modeled:
Scenario,Trigger,Duration,ImpactEstimate,Mitigation
TransientBurst90s,load spike from batch warmup,90s,~+40% token throughput power -> need 15% spillway,enable staging queue and token rate-limit for latency-critical routes
PDUFailureSingle,rack PDU dies,indefinite,reduce per-rack GPU count on that rack -> migrate lowest-priority replicas to sibling racks; enable power-based autoshed
CRACLoopDegradation,CRAC performance drops 20%,>10min,alarm for thermal threshold -> trigger cooling handoff to neighboring loop and shift mid-weight models off affected racks

Recommendation (balanced):
- Slot distribution (balanced): put 20 cards into A3 (empty), 10 into A1, 6 into A6, 4 into A4, 2 into A5, 6 into A2 (total 48). Rationale: uses empty rack first, avoids overloading A2/A5, keeps per-rack PDU utilization <72% post-deploy with 15% spillway reserved.
- Configure capacity controller: set per-rack transient headroom policy = 15% thermal, power-based autoshed at 80% of PDU available (pre-failure), route latency tolerant traffic to racks A3 & A6 when average CPU queue depth > threshold.
- Short-term procurement: start quote for an additional 16U cage (estimate 6 kW usable after PDUs) if Q1 growth exceeds forecast.

Monitoring / Dashboard checklist to validate after deploy:
- Per-rack PDU power (1s sampling), 1m, 5m, 1h aggregate panels
- Inlet/outlet air delta per rack, CRAC loop flow rate, and floor temp sensors in 3 heights per rack
- Alerts: sustained >12% over baseline for 5m, instantaneous >25% for 30s, PDU current imbalance >15A differential across phases
- Canary prompts: after each slotting change, run a 10-minute synthetic load to validate thermal bleed and redispatch policies. Add a run to the deploy checklist.

Cost & procurement quick numbers (est):
- If we need additional PDUs for A3: 2x redundant PDUs (3kW each effective) ~ $18k installed (colo fee + install)
- Temporary extra rack quote (3U PDUs + basic cooling tie-in) ~ $12k one-time + $300/month cage space

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we accept 72% per-rack utilization post-deploy as operational baseline? (ops SLA tradeoff)
- Approve procurement path for temporary rack if Q1 forecast > 10% ingress.
- Confirm routing policy in Redwood controller: allow cross-rack burst routing for inference-hosted-prod (yes/no).

Action items (owners):
- Asha: finalize slotting plan and update deployment playbook by 2026-09-30.
- Liam: schedule PDU install quote and run single-rack PDU failure drill 2026-09-10 -> 2026-09-20.
- Marisol: add thermal sensors to A5 & A4 and wire into Grafana (ticket: JIRA-INFRA-4123).
- Jonah: update capacity-controller configs (spillway target, cross-rack routing rules) in PR #278 and request review.

Notes / fringe thoughts (scratchpad):
- Consider aggressive quantization profiles for latency-bound models to reduce thermal draw per token (tradeoff quality). If quantization reduces average GPU power by 25% we gain ~10 extra practical slots without hardware changes.
- If colo will offer additional 40 kW in Jan 2027 at 20% discount, factor into Q1 planning for permanent expansion rather than temporary rack moves.
- Keep a small manual reserve of low-priority inference replicas that can be offlined first during any thermal events.

History / context links:
- Aug 2026 power sweep measurements (Asha): acoustic+thermal logs attached to Confluence page above.
- Previous rack-density playbook (engineering/private-deployments/gpu-rack-tiling-and-cooling-playbook-2025-11) consulted but this sheet takes a spillway-first approach rather than pure density.

End of sheet.
